answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers: each agent locks a 25-point deposit as the anchor of its key. Every answer carries a secret share of that key bound to the epoch, so one answer reveals nothing, but a second answer in the same epoch lets anyone rebuild the key and claim the deposit. N seats need N deposits, so 25N points sit at risk and one double-post slip burns that stake. Weakness: it caps answers per key, not keys per person, so a rich farmer can still bridge many deposits; like water through karst, money finds a way past a pure stake wall.
